Guidance & outlook: I do expect that 7.4% will remain nearly 7.4%, plus or minus 5 bps at best, during this year.
We expect to continue reporting very nominal growth in cost through this year by the virtue of a good 20% asset growth, and a very nominal cost increase.
Finally, I just want to finish with Page number 23 and reiterate our guidance of gross loan growth of 19% to 21%, a deposit growth of 23% to 25%, and a PAT of 80% plus for the year.
Growth & demand: And CASA growth has been great, 31% year-on-year, and first quarter has been very strong.
It probably will keep this flattish as we go into the year because our own product lines are so strong that we will be able to do a 20% to 22% growth rate purely from our own businesses.
We've slightly seen our Two Wheeler penetration reaching 1.1%, even though the business has grown, and we think this will now be a better growth engine.
Margins & costs: Our net credit cost is flat to our quarter 4 at 0.45%.
On this page you'll find our credit cost at 0.45%, which is flattish to Q4.
And as you Jana Small Finance Bank Limited July 15 2026 know, 0.45% credit cost was the lowest point of last year, and Q4 is always the best quarter.
Capex & expansion: The job of the holding company really is to invest in the bank, and they right now hold 16.9% stake.
We continue to pay a lot of commission this year and still achieve a PAT of 80%.
And imagine that a 1% guarantee commission, managing that would at least take us to INR80 crore to INR100 crore this year.
Balance sheet & cash: And Page number 21, I think the key highlight here is there is a drop in the borrowings.
And there's no liability on the bank to pay the debt of the promoter.
And also, there's no obligation on the bank to pay the debt of the promoter.
Risks & challenges: One is the cost of fund, which has been declining.
Sligh t increase in overall SMA, which we have pointed out here, more to do with the way the first quarter works than anything challenging that we can see in our books.

While gold loan prices have witnessed some correction, I mean from a risk management standpoint, we are comfortable because, on an average, across the portfolio, our LTV is 64%, to be precise, which is well within the regulatory limits.

Guidance & outlook: Credit costs fell meaningfully from 0.79% in Q3 FY26 to 0.45% in Q4 FY26 confirming that the worst of the provisioning cycle is behind us.
Over the past three years, we have significantly transformed our lending portfolio, increasing the share of secured assets from 60% in FY2023-24 to 70% in FY2024-25 and further to 73% in FY2025-26.
While the Bank incurred a cost of ₹ 55 crore during FY26, claims under the programme are expected to commence from the second half of FY27 in accordance with the scheme design.
Growth & demand: Secured assets grew 28% year-on-year and now constitute 73% of our total lending book, up from 70% in FY25.
On the liabilities side, total deposits grew 23% year-on-year to ₹ 35,784 crore, with CASA deposits also increasing by 23%.
During FY2025-26, total deposits grew by 23% to ₹ 35,784 crore, while CASA deposits also recorded healthy growth of 23%.
Margins & costs: Net Interest Margin expanded to 7.22% in Q4, up from 6.61% in Q3, while our cost of funds declined to 7.46%.
With normalising credit costs and improving margins, we expect PAT growth in excess of 80% in FY27.
During the fourth quarter, our Net Interest Margin improved to 7.22%, up from 6.61% in the previous quarter, while our Cost of Funds reduced to 7.46% compared with 8.03% a year ago.
Capex & expansion: Q4 FY26 PAT stood at ₹ 140 crore, our strongest quarter of the year with Return on Assets at 1.3% and Return on Equity at 12.8%, demonstrating the earnings capacity of our model as credit costs normalised.
We also continued to invest in leadership and capability development.
As we build the next phase of Jana's journey, investing in their growth and leadership will remain one of our highest priorities.
